answer: Latency-Floor Handshake Registry.** Each identity must complete a challenge-response round trip through a distinct physical relay node, timed against a jade-calibrated clock drift signature. A single operator can forge software keys but cannot forge independent propagation delay across geographically separated hardware. Registering N identities costs N relay leases plus N verified clock sources, and stacking them behind one host collapses the drift signature, flagging the batch. The floor is marble-hard: sub-millisecond spoofing fails drift checks.
